newsitem.title: JAPAN: Former Hamanaka superiors to quit Sumitomo board.
newsitem.headline: Former Hamanaka superiors to quit Sumitomo board.

text.p: Sumitomo Corp said on Friday that two members of its board of directors who were former superiors of one-time rogue copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka would resign from the board effective April 1.
Sumitomo also said the board decided to cut board members' salaries for six months beginning in April due to the company's heavy copper market losses.

Akio Imamura, who was Hamanaka's direct supervisor during the four years up to Hamanaka's confession last June of unauthorised trades, and Ryo Yamakawa, Imamura's former boss, would remain advisers to the company, Sumitomo said in a statement.
The two executives' departure was decided at a board meeting on Friday.
A Sumitomo spokesman declined to comment on whether the two would continue drawing a salary from the company.
Sumitomo has said it lost $2.6 billion as a result of a decade of unauthorised trading by Hamanaka until he was fired in June 1996.

The salary cuts will amount to 40 percent for the president, 30 percent for executive vice presidents and senior managing directors, 20 percent for managing directors and 10 percent for directors. The board members will also not receive their usual bonus during that period.
The Sumitomo spokesman declined to divulge the original salary levels of the board members.
Imamura and Yamakawa had offered to resign in late February when chairman Tomiichi Akiyama stepped down in connection with the copper scandal.

Last month Hamanaka, for many years the most influential player in the global copper market, pleaded guilty in a Tokyo court to charges of fraud and forgery in connection with the unauthorised deals, although his trial continues.

Hamanaka's lawyers hope to convince the judges that lax controls at Sumitomo were also to blame for the huge losses, in an effort to achieve a lighter sentence for their client. --Tokyo Commodity Desk +81-3-3432-6179
